Hawaii Code AI-Thon: how it works, in 60 seconds

You don't need to know how to code. You need to describe what you want, and give it feedback.

Make first. Code later. You are the project manager: you describe, test and steer. The AI is the developer: it writes the code.

Step 1, frame it: start with a real problem. "I need a way to track my homework so I never miss a due date." Plus three simple features: class and task, due date, check it off.

Step 2, generate: paste the Super Prompt into Gemini Canvas, add your idea, and see a working Homework Tracker app appear in about a minute.

Step 3, test and steer: small steps, small fixes. The Add button is stuck, so you type "Fix the Add button.", Gemini works on it, and it works. Then "Switch the theme." One change at a time.

Step 4, ship it: share a real link. Export to Google Sites, share to Classroom, or publish on GitHub Pages. The app opens in a browser and on a phone.

What will you make? A tip splitter, flashcards, a lunch picker, a habit tracker, a study timer. You can just make digital things.

Hawaii Code AI-Thon. Coming February 2027: one week, one theme. Open the guide, pick an idea, start tinkering now: lpcode808.github.io/Hawaii-Code-AI-Thon-Help. Use a personal Google account.
